rule.explanation: This control requires disabling direct SSH login as root. PermitRootLogin without-password prohibits root password and keyboard-interactive authentication but can still permit public-key authentication. PermitRootLogin no disables direct root SSH login. Administrative access through another account and authorized privilege elevation must be assessed separately.

attack.relationship: Conditional restriction of one local-account access path
attack.justification: An adversary possessing usable credentials for the local root account could abuse direct root SSH access when that access is permitted. Disabling it restricts this particular route; it does not prevent abuse of other local accounts or other routes to root.
attack.conditions: SSH must be reachable, the applicable SSH configuration must permit root authentication, and the adversary must satisfy the authentication and account-access requirements. A failed compliance check alone does not establish these conditions.

rule.limitation: This mapping is a project-authored interpretation, not an official CIS-to-ATT&CK mapping.
No CVE applicability is established by this configuration finding.
A passing result does not establish that all SSH access or local-account abuse is prevented.
rule.verification: Compare the selected scan result with the saved effective SSH configuration and corresponding root-login and administrative-access test logs. Account for connection-specific Match settings. OpenSSH setting reference: https://man.openbsd.org/sshd_config#PermitRootLogin
